About S8UL

S8UL is an Indian esports and gaming content organisation based in Mumbai. It was formed in 2020 when Team SouL, owned by Naman "Mortal" Mathur, joined hands with 8Bit Creatives, founded by Animesh "Thug" Agarwal and Lokesh "Goldy" Jain.

S8UL first made its name in PUBG Mobile and BGMI, then expanded into Valorant, Pokémon UNITE, Call of Duty, Apex Legends, Chess, Tekken and EA FC. Today it competes in 18 titles across mobile, PC and console. Alongside the results, it built one of India's largest gaming content ecosystems on YouTube and live streaming.

At the Esports Awards, S8UL has won Esports Content Group of the Year four times.

The Gaming House

S8UL Gaming House 2.0 in Mumbai is home to around 25 creators. The four-floor, 15,000 sq ft facility is valued at about $1 million and has streaming cabins, living rooms, recreation areas, a kitchen and content creation spaces.

The journey of S8UL

From a single team in 2018 to one of India's biggest esports and content brands, year by year.

  • 2018 · The beginning

    Team SouL is founded. This is the root of everything S8UL would become.

  • 2019 · First big wins

    Team SouL wins PMIS 2019 and PMCO India 2019 in PUBG Mobile.

  • 2020 · S8UL is born

    Team SouL and 8Bit Creatives merge. Naman "Mortal" Mathur, Animesh "Thug" Agarwal and Lokesh "Goldy" Jain join forces, and S8UL begins.

  • 2021 · Beyond one game

    S8UL launches its VALORANT and Free Fire teams and keeps growing its creator family.

  • 2022 · Champions

    Team SouL wins BMPS 2022. S8UL wins Esports Content Group of the Year at the Esports Awards for the first time.

  • 2023 · Content king, UNITE champion

    Content Group of the Year again, and the first Pokémon UNITE Championship Series India title.

  • 2024 · Three in a row

    A third Content Group of the Year, the MOBIES Mobile Gaming award and a second Pokémon UNITE India title.

  • 2025 · Going global

    S8UL becomes the first and only Indian organisation in the Esports World Cup Foundation Club Partner Program, and represents India at the Esports World Cup in Riyadh. It also wins a fourth Content Group of the Year, a third Pokémon UNITE India title and the Legends Ascend South Asia title in League of Legends, and signs top chess grandmasters.

  • 2026 · The comeback year

    Team SouL wins BGIS 2026 and ends a four-year wait for an official title. S8UL adds a fourth Pokémon UNITE India title, the VALORANT VCSA Split 1 title and a chess win at Dreamhack Atlanta, and is selected as an Esports World Cup Club Partner again.

  • Today

    18 esports titles, 30+ creators, 250+ brand partners and a Gaming House in Mumbai.

The rocket is running, and it is not slowing down. 🚀
